# Ibd

This folder catalogs the specific clinical quality indicators used by the Dansk Kvalitetsdatabase for Inflammatoriske Tarmsygdomme (DANIBD) to monitor and evaluate the standard of care for inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) and related conditions in Denmark. The indicators span the entire patient journey, tracking diagnostic workups for both adult and pediatric patients, postoperative endoscopic follow-ups, patient education, biological treatment monitoring, surgical re-operation rates, and surveillance for comorbidities like primary sclerosing cholangitis (PSC). Together, these pages detail the national fulfillment rates, regional variations, and critical feedback from hospital departments regarding the clinical validity and data capture mechanisms of each metric.

## Pages

- [[indikator-1]] — Evaluates the quality of IBD patient investigations, though criticized by Aarhus Universitetshospital for skewed metrics caused by suboptimal data capture.
- [[indikator-1a|Indikator 1a]] — Tracks the proportion of newly diagnosed adult IBD patients receiving a colonoscopy within 12 months of their first hospital contact.
- [[indikator-1b|Indikator 1b]] — Measures the completion of comprehensive diagnostic workups, including gastroscopy, colonoscopy, and MRI, for newly diagnosed pediatric IBD patients.
- [[indikator-2|Indikator 2]] — Monitors the delivery of structured patient education to newly diagnosed IBD patients within one year of diagnosis, highlighting initial low registration rates.
- [[indikator-3|Indikator 3]] — Assesses postoperative care by measuring the proportion of adult Crohn's disease patients who undergo a colonoscopy within a year of an ileocecal resection.
- [[indikator-4|Indikator 4]] — Tracks the annual measurement of fecal calprotectin for IBD patients on biological therapies, with regional notes also referencing DEXA scans for steroid-treated patients.
- [[indikator-5|Indikator 5]] — Monitors annual fecal calprotectin measurements for IBD patients treated with biological and targeted synthetic drugs (BMSL), successfully reaching its national development goal.
- [[indikator-6|Indikator 6]] — Measures the 30-day re-operation rate following primary IBD surgeries, serving as a surgical quality proxy despite criticism from some hospitals regarding its clinical validity.
- [[indikator-7|Indikator 7]] — Evaluates the systematic surveillance of adults with primary sclerosing cholangitis (PSC) by tracking colonoscopies performed within an 18-month window.
